title: Peak lumbar back EMG lifting 10 kg from ankle height with free, squat and stoop technique, no exoskeleton

quantity.name: peak lumbar back EMG
quantity.definition: peak over lift of normalised EMG averaged over IL and LL and sides; mean ± SD (error bars assumed SD). Values >100% because MVC was obtained in supine maximal efforts

source.authors: Koopman AS, Näf M, Baltrusch SJ, Kingma I, Rodriguez-Guerrero C, Babič J, de Looze MP, van Dieën JH

protocol.summary: Lifting a 10 kg box with handles 10 cm above ankle height (horizontal distance not stated) using three techniques: Free (self-selected), Squat (knees flexed, trunk upright), Stoop (trunk bent, knees extended); cycle = pick up, return upright holding box, replace, return upright; 3 reps each; self-selected speed; WITHOUT exoskeleton only. Peak values. Bilateral surface EMG: rectus abdominis (RA), external oblique (EO), iliocostalis (IL), longissimus thoracis (TL), longissimus pars lumborum (LL), sites per Kingma et al. 2010 (levels/distances not stated). Lumbar back = average of IL and LL (and sides); abdominal = average of RA and EO. Normalisation %MVC; MVCs for back and abdominal muscles in supine posture (McGill 1991); band-pass 20-600 Hz, rectified, low-pass 2.5 Hz.
how_to_simulate: Scale model to a 175 cm, 83.6 kg male
Simulate 10 kg box lifts from 10 cm above ankle height with the three techniques (peak lumbar flexion 54-64 deg)
Compare peak mean activation of iliocostalis + longissimus lumborum

subject_model.source: Koopman 2020b Methods 2.2 (mean of 10 males; 1.75 ± 0.07 m, 83.6 ± 16.2 kg)

protocol.notes: WITHOUT digitised (Fig. 4): peak lumbar flexion Free 56.5±7.5, Squat 53.7±6.1, Stoop 63.5±8.9 deg; peak trunk angular velocity Free 209±51, Squat 184±25, Stoop 177±34 deg/s.
